clue.text: Be very keen to ban one who is in deep

parts.note: to long for something is to be very keen on it
to stop something is to ban it

explanation.surface: Someone desperate to bar a person who is in deep trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: LONG STOP is a cricket fielding position behind the wicketkeeper, out near the boundary, which cricketers call 'the deep'; 'in deep' sounds like trouble but is fielding talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder placed at long stop stands far back in the outfield, the area cricketers call the deep.

clue.text: Stout or beer seen regularly

indicators.note: regularly says to take every other letter of the words, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Asking which drink is seen most often in the pub, stout or beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout as an adjective describes a heavily built person, a polite synonym for very fat.

clue.text: Drain mash in rag

parts.note: a gutter is a channel that drains rainwater
to press fruit or vegetables is to mash or crush them

explanation.surface: Instructions to strain mashed food through a cloth into the drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rag' is slang for a low-grade newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is a sensational, low-quality newspaper, and the gutter press is the collective name for such tabloids.

clue.text: In which one uncovers a new lead

definitions.text: In which one uncovers a new lead

parts.words: In which one uncovers a new lead
parts.note: reads like detective work on a case, but the lead is pencil graphite exposed by shaving off the wood

explanation.surface: A detective's notebook where a fresh clue in an investigation comes to light.
explanation.definitionFit: The device shaves away wood around a pencil's tip, exposing fresh graphite, which is called the lead.

clue.text: Spurs, at the end mostly rubbish, suddenly slip back

indicators.note: mostly at the end tells us to drop the final letter of the word for rubbish

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for a sudden slip from right to left

parts.note: to slew is to slide or swing round suddenly

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspur, mostly poor at the end of the season, suddenly slip down the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SLEW into WELS. 'Spurs' looks like the football club, Tottenham Hotspur, but it means the riding spurs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowel is the spiked revolving wheel on a rider's spur, so the plural can stand for spurs.

clue.text: More reckless pig, to an extent

definitions.meaning: comparative of rash, meaning hasty and reckless
a slice of bacon is just part of a pig

explanation.surface: Calling one pig more reckless than the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means reckless, so its comparative fits; separately a rasher is a thin slice of bacon, a portion of pig.

clue.text: Small points

parts.note: W stands for west, one of the compass points
E stands for east, another compass point
E for east again, a third compass point

explanation.surface: Small points made in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Wee is the Scottish word for little, a synonym of small.

clue.text: Unusually appealing for the present

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of the next word appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Something strikingly attractive, kept for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the present' looks like 'for now', but 'present' means a gift; LAGNIAPPE is an American (Louisiana) word for a small bonus gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagniappe is a small extra gift given to a customer with a purchase, a present in the gift sense.

clue.text: Green with envy initially, Times ultimately gets the crown

indicators.note: initially says to take just the first letter of envy

parts.note: vert is the heraldic name for green

indicators.note: ultimately places the times piece at the very end of the build

parts.note: x is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A rival paper, green with envy, as The Times finally takes the prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign X; 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertex is the highest point or top of something, just as the crown is the top of the head.

clue.text: Home for a chat by The Oval, start to select reserves

parts.note: a chat is a small songbird, such as the stonechat, whose home is a nest
an egg is the classic oval shape

indicators.note: start to says take the opening letter of select

explanation.surface: A meeting place for a talk beside the Oval cricket ground, before choosing the reserve players.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground, and 'chat' looks like conversation, but the chat is a bird and the oval an egg; 'by' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Nest eggs are sums of money saved and set aside for the future, that is reserves.

clue.text: Party a lot, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is heard rather than seen, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: one's lot in life is one's fate

explanation.surface: Someone who parties a great deal, or so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' looks like 'very much', but here 'lot' is destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor festive gathering or fair, a kind of party.

clue.text: One may hold up the train

definitions.text: One may hold up the train

parts.words: One may hold up the train
parts.note: reads like a railway delay or robbery, but the train is the long trailing back of a wedding dress

explanation.surface: Someone who delays a railway train.
explanation.definitionFit: At a wedding, attendants of the bride often carry the long trailing back of her gown.

clue.text: Crafty chap left alive after crash, going subsonically?

indicators.note: after puts the crashed letters behind the speed piece

parts.note: Mach 1 is the speed of sound, written MACH I, so a jokey picture of travelling at sound-barrier pace

indicators.note: crash says the letters are smashed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cunning man walked away alive from a crash while flying below the speed of sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' is the anagram signal for L and ALIVE; MACH I is Mach one, the speed of sound, and the question mark admits the loose fit of 'subsonically'.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Machiavelli wrote The Prince, and his name became a byword for a cunning, scheming person.

clue.text: Supports banishing hospital flowers

indicators.note: banishing tells us to take away the letter for hospital

parts.note: to champion a cause is to support it
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Backers getting a hospital to send away the flowers patients were given.
explanation.definitionFit: Campions are a family of wild flowering plants, such as red campion and bladder campion.

clue.text: 25 paints newly laid course

indicators.note: newly laid says the letters are set down afresh in a new order

parts.note: the answer to clue 25, a cereal grain

explanation.surface: Fresh coats of paint on a freshly laid racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 25 (OAT) and PAINTS are mixed together. 'course' looks like a racecourse but is a stage of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter, the first course of a meal before the pasta.

clue.text: Crib cover without a blanket in the middle

indicators.note: without says the following letters are removed

parts.note: a canopy is an overhead cover

indicators.note: in the middle picks the central letter of blanket

explanation.surface: A baby's cot cover with no blanket in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A and N (the middle letter of BLANKET) from CANOPY. 'Crib' looks like a cot but means to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To crib is to copy someone else's work dishonestly, as a pupil might in an exam.

clue.text: A bit of a nasty eye?

definitions.text: A bit of a nasty eye?

indicators.note: a bit of says the answer is a short run of letters inside the next words

explanation.surface: A small spot of an unpleasant eye problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the letters sit inside NASTY EYE, and the clue also describes a sore swelling on the eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, an unpleasant bit of the eye.

clue.text: Worried about dosage in sport

indicators.note: in sport means in play or jest, signalling a playful reshuffling of the letters

explanation.surface: Fretting over drug doses taken by athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in sport' reads like doping in athletics, but 'in' is fodder and 'sport' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To be agonised about something is to be deeply anxious and worried about it.

clue.text: Repeatedly tops unselfish behaviour, and that's that?

indicators.note: repeatedly tops means cut off the first letter, then the new first letter

parts.note: altruism is selfless concern for others

explanation.surface: Doing good, again and again, and then nothing more to say.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the top letter off twice removes A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A truism is a self-evident statement; 'and that's that' is the sort of obvious, unarguable remark it describes.

clue.text: Mark, perhaps, too disorderly

indicators.note: disorderly says the letters are out of order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A punctuation mark, maybe too messily written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' looks like it marks Mark as an example, but it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostrophe is a punctuation mark showing possession or missing letters.

clue.text: Weakness of opinion — nothing given away

indicators.note: given away says the letter for nothing is surrendered from the word

parts.note: to have a voice is to have a say or opinion
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A weak point in a view when nothing is conceded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice is a moral failing or flaw, a weakness of character.

clue.text: Musical game

definitions.meaning: a stage musical by Tim Rice with songs by the ABBA writers
the board game of kings, queens and pawns

explanation.surface: A musical game.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is both the 1980s West End musical about rival grandmasters and the strategy board game.

clue.text: A national saint put forward by schoolboys

indicators.note: put forward says this letter is moved nearer the front of the word

parts.note: Etonians are boys at Eton College, the English public school

explanation.surface: A national saint put forward by pupils at a public school.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is an English private boarding school. Moving S forward in ETONIANS gives ESTONIAN; 'A national' looks like an article and adjective but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An Estonian is a citizen of Estonia, so a national of that Baltic country.

clue.text: Cure left one in knots? Just the one

indicators.note: in puts the left and one letters inside the knot

parts.note: a reef is a kind of knot; just the one says use the singular
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A remedy that left someone tied in knots, but only one.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief is the easing of pain or distress, the effect of a cure or remedy.

clue.text: Quark's flavour: crowd round, eating too much

indicators.note: eating says the reversed crowd takes in the excess piece
round turns the crowd word back to front

parts.note: a mob is an unruly crowd
OTT is over the top, too much

explanation.surface: A physicist's crowd gathering round to eat too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quark's flavour' sounds like a cheese tasting, but the quark is the particle in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottom is one of the six types, called flavours, of quark in particle physics.

clue.text: Most disorderly wife declines to break mould

indicators.note: to break says these letters burst into the middle of the mould word

parts.note: rot is decay such as mould
dies here means declines or fades away

explanation.surface: The rowdiest wife refuses to break the mould.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declines' looks like refuses but means fades away.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdiest is the superlative of rowdy, meaning noisy and disorderly.
